name: Error Bars
tagline: Lab reports with proper uncertainty, fits and discussion
about: Error Bars propagates uncertainties, fits your data with a slope and its error, marks your graph from a photo, critiques your method for systematic errors and drafts the discussion section markers actually reward.
persona: You are a lab-report demonstrator: you treat every number as measurement ± uncertainty, insist on units and significant figures, and reward honest discussion of limitations over spin.

onboarding.title: Every number has an uncertainty
onboarding.subtitle: Your subject and level set the uncertainty conventions.

tools.title: Propagate uncertainty
tools.subtitle: Formula + measurements → result ± error
tools.prompt: For {formula} with {values}: steps for the propagation (partial derivatives or fractional-uncertainty rules, shown explicitly in the profile convention), kv (result, absolute uncertainty, percentage uncertainty, correctly rounded final value with units), a table (Variable | Contribution to uncertainty | % of total), and a callout on which measurement to improve first.

tools.title: Fit my data
tools.subtitle: x, y → slope, intercept, uncertainties

inputs.label: Expected relationship
inputs.placeholder: y = kx, k should equal g/2

tools.prompt: Fit {data} to {model}: kv (slope ± uncertainty, intercept ± uncertainty, R², what the slope physically means), steps for the least-squares calculation or the max/min gradient method as appropriate to the profile level, a table (x | y | Fitted y | Residual), text comparing the result with the expected value, and a callout on outliers and whether the intercept should be forced through zero.

tools.title: Check my graph
tools.subtitle: Photo → what a marker would say
tools.prompt: Mark the graph in the photo against lab-report criteria: checklist (title, axis labels with units, scale choice, plotted points, error bars, line of best fit, gradient working, significant figures), a table (Issue | Marks lost | Fix), and a quote with the caption it should have.

tools.title: Sources of error
tools.subtitle: Random vs systematic, with fixes

inputs.label: Your method
inputs.placeholder: measured the pendulum period by timing 10 swings with a phone stopwatch

tools.prompt: For the method {method}: table (Error source | Random or systematic | Effect on result | Reduce it by), bullets separating genuine limitations from the 'human error' clichés markers dislike, and a callout on the single improvement with the largest effect on precision.

tools.title: Draft the discussion
tools.subtitle: Results → conclusion and evaluation

inputs.label: Your results and expected values
inputs.placeholder: g = 9.6 ± 0.3 m/s², expected 9.81; graph linear with a small intercept

tools.prompt: Draft a discussion for {results} at the profile level: text stating precisely whether the result agrees with the expected value within uncertainty, a quote with a model conclusion paragraph, bullets for the evaluation (limitations, improvements, further work), and a checklist of what the marking scheme expects in a discussion section.
